questions.prompt: Which statement allocates room on the heap for a copy of the string "Hello"?
questions.explain: A string needs one extra byte for the terminating `'\0'`: 5 letters + 1 = 6 bytes. `char s[6]` is stack (not heap) memory and the literal is read-only static data.
option_notes: One byte short: the terminator would overflow the block.
That is an array on the stack, not heap memory.
That only points to a string literal; nothing is allocated.

questions.prompt: `free` must receive a pointer that was returned by `malloc`, `calloc` or {{0}}.
questions.explain: Freeing anything else (a stack address, a pointer into the middle of a block, a pointer already freed) is undefined behaviour.

questions.prompt: `calloc(n, size)` differs from `malloc` because it sets all the bytes it returns to {{0}}.
questions.explain: `malloc` leaves the memory uninitialised (garbage); `calloc` zero-fills it.

questions.prompt: Put these steps in order to grow a heap array safely.
items: Call realloc and keep the result in a temporary pointer
Check that the temporary pointer is not NULL
Assign the temporary pointer to the array pointer
questions.explain: If you wrote `v = realloc(v, n)` directly and it failed, `v` would become NULL and the old block would leak. Using a temporary keeps the original pointer valid on failure.
